thread.title: State Board of Education reviews strategic plan and approves new charter school

author: T. R. Rhodes
title: State Board of Education reviews strategic plan and approves new charter school
text:
The State Board of Education received an update on a revised student-centered strategic plan from the Missouri Department of Elementary and Secondary Education and approved a five-year charter application for Frontier STEM Academy – Elementary in Columbia at its meeting on April 16.
The review of the department’s strategic plan matters because it sets priorities that affect students, schools, and communities across Missouri. The department manages public education for kindergarten through twelfth grade as well as early childhood initiatives, according to the official website.
Commissioner of Education Dr. Karla Eslinger presented an initial draft of the updated strategic plan alongside technical assistance providers. This was the first opportunity for board members to discuss and provide feedback to help shape the direction of education in Missouri. Over seven months, the department used stakeholder surveys, work groups, and national landscape scans to develop recommendations for this revision. The priorities include strengthening academic foundations with great teaching, focusing support on underperforming schools and districts, building kindergarten readiness, preparing students for postsecondary success, developing quality data systems to drive decision-making, and fostering strong attendance in safe and healthy schools.
“All Missouri students are capable of success and deserve a strong educational foundation that equips them to reach this potential,” said Dr. Eslinger. “Delivering on that promise requires clear priorities, consistent focus, and coordinated action across our state.” The department serves all 557 public school districts and charter schools statewide according to its official website.
In other business at the meeting, the board approved a five-year charter application for Frontier STEM Academy – Elementary in Columbia. The school plans to open within Columbia Public School District boundaries during the 2027-28 year with Pre-K through grade two classes before expanding by one grade each year until serving Pre-K through grade five.
The next State Board meeting is scheduled for May 12 in St. Louis. The Missouri Department of Elementary and Secondary Education supports school accountability through programs such as the Missouri School Improvement Program according to its official website. It also coordinates federal programs like Title I and Title IV funding according to its official website.
